Upstream exposes a pure JavaScript BPE encoder/decoder, token-count and token-limit APIs, chat accounting helpers and model cost estimates; its default encoding is o200k_base. These are measurement/encoding functions, not automatic prompt reduction.

Upstream calls itself the fastest tokenizer on npm and links its own encoding/decoding, initialization and memory benchmarks. That is a library-runtime performance claim, not evidence of fewer provider tokens in this adaptation.

limitations.text: No CLI executable is shipped: package.json at tag 4.0.0 has no bin field and provides ESM/CommonJS exports. The published npm manifest also has no bin (https://registry.npmjs.org/gpt-tokenizer/4.0.0). A consumer running node -e is invoking the library, not a gpt-tokenizer subprocess binary.

The tagged source package.json uses the release-build placeholder version 0.0.0; use GitHub release/tag and published npm metadata for release identity rather than treating that placeholder as the installed version.

Text encoding is not a complete model request or billing meter. Upstream distinguishes encode/countTokens from model-aware chat accounting and cost estimation; model metadata or an encoding choice does not verify Claude or Codex provider usage.

Special tokens are disallowed by default and may make encoding throw unless the caller explicitly chooses a handling policy. The documented local LRU merge cache accelerates tokenization; it is not provider prompt caching.
Image-token accounting remains an open upstream issue; ordinary text-artifact counts should not be represented as complete multimodal request accounting.
The major update removes UMD bundles and the unpkg global entry point. ESM/CommonJS remain available, but consumer import/build compatibility still needs qualification.
